item.research_question: What is the feasibility of using a Si-20Cr-20Fe coating to improve the oxidation resistance of MoNbTaTiW refractory high-entropy alloys, and how do the microstructure and composition of the coating evolve during high-temperature oxidation?
item.material_system: MoNbTaTiW refractory high-entropy alloy (RHEA) substrate with a Si-20Cr-20Fe (wt.%) silicide coating
item.processing_route: Fused slurry method: Si-20Cr-20Fe powder mixed with 4% polyethylene alcohol binder, applied to polished RHEA cuboids, dried at 80 °C, then vacuum annealed at 1430 °C for 1 h under 5 × 10−3 Pa
item.test_conditions: Oxidation in static air at 1000 °C and 1300 °C for 1 h with a heating rate of 10 °C/min
key_findings: The initial silicide coating had a double-layer structure with an outer MSi2 layer (66.2 at.% Si) and an inner M5Si3 layer (37.9 at.% Si).
The initial coating thickness was ~113 µm, increasing to 347 µm after oxidation at 1000 °C and 397 µm after oxidation at 1300 °C.
After oxidation at 1000 °C, the coating developed a three-layer structure (two silicide layers, one oxide layer) with a gap between the oxide and silicide layers.
After oxidation at 1300 °C, the coating developed a four-layer structure (two silicide layers, two oxide layers) with no gap between the oxide and silicide layers.
The outer oxide layer at 1000 °C consisted of SiO2, TiO2, Cr2SiO4, Ta0.3W0.7O2.85, and Ti0.67Nb1.33O4.
The outer oxide layer at 1300 °C consisted of CrNbO4, SiO2, WO3, and Fe2SiO4, with no Mo or Ta oxides detected.
Silicon diffused from the coating into the substrate, causing the silicide layer to move inward while its thickness increased significantly (e.g., L2 layer grew from 67 µm to 181 µm at 1000 °C).
The L1 layer (M5Si3) thickness decreased from ~46 µm to ~33 µm (1000 °C) and ~34 µm (1300 °C), while the L2 layer (MSi2) thickness more than doubled.
item.mechanism: Silicon diffused from the silicide coating into the RHEA substrate during oxidation, causing the silicide layer to move toward the substrate and increase in thickness. The oxide layer formed on the surface, with its structure and composition depending on temperature; at 1300 °C, complete oxidation of metals and silicon, combined with the volatilization of oxides like MoO3, resulted in a stable oxide layer volume without gaps, whereas at 1000 °C, volume expansion caused bulging and gaps.
item.limitations: The text does not explicitly state limitations of the study.
item.future_work: The text does not explicitly state future work.
quotes: The initial silicide coating had a double-layer structure: a high silicon content layer mainly composed of MSi2 as the outer layer and a low silicon content layer mainly contained M5Si3 as the inner layer.
Under high-temperature oxidation conditions, the silicon element diffused from the silicide coating to the RHEA substrate while the oxidation of the coating occurred.
The structure and compositions of the oxide layer on the outer surface strongly depended on the oxidation temperature.
